Treatment summary
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which their vehicle was struck from the side while the patient
was turning left. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the type and force of the impact. Presenting
complaints involved the right knee, with pain, swelling, and limited range of motion. Imaging and physical examination
findings clearly confirm the knee injury, and the patient's history reveals no prior injury to the same area.
Conservative management was provided over twelve visits, consisting of physical therapy, joint mobilization,
progressive strengthening, and home exercise instruction. Recovery was somewhat slower than typically expected
for this type of injury, and the course of care extended beyond the usual timeframe. Billing records reflect single
entries for each service without duplicate charges. At the most recent evaluation, the patient had improved in strength
and mobility but still reported intermittent discomfort with stairs and prolonged standing. Continued home exercise
and activity modification were recommended.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
